Ellie Ward was a witness at the trial. Simon’s sentence, ‘Are you saying Ellie wasn’t there?’, was read out from the record. Ellie went to Martin’s funeral; she spoke to no one.
The defence proved Simon had never known Martin; because of the missing motive, the charge was reduced to manslaughter by negligence.
With no target sought, the file stayed within the frame of negligence; why Simon went into that room was never explained.
No link was found between Tom and either Simon or the room; that question weakened the file.
The engineer’s licence was suspended for the duration of the investigation, then restored. The real culprit was not sought.
Simon Pryce was arrested for murder and fraud. The cloth in the flue turned out to be from the same batch as the cleaning cloths in the office van.
The file was closed as an accident. Harbour Lettings handed management of the house to another officer.
Victor Crane was tried for negligence; the engineer’s report brought the charge down at the first hearing. Simon Pryce went on managing three more houses.

THE TENANT  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH

In a shared rented house in Deptford, a man is found dead from carbon monoxide leaking from the fire in his room. A house with an expired certificate, a landlord with complaints. First note: negligence.

At 08.40 on 23 March 2029, Tom Becker, who lives at 14 Ashgrove Road, Deptford, called 999 with a severe headache and nausea. The attending crew found that no gas alarm had sounded in the house, but that the carbon monoxide reading in room 3 upstairs was very high.

A man was found motionless in bed in the room; he was pronounced dead at the scene. According to the ID in his wallet, Martin Hughes (52). The gas fire in the room was on and the window was shut.

Becker was taken to hospital; his condition is good.

Patrol note: “It was learned that the house’s gas safety certificate expired in February and that the landlord had previously received two tenant complaints. Negligence is the priority line.”

The engineer’s 9 March report showed the flue clear; at the scene the flue was blocked with a cloth. According to the key log, the only recorded person who entered the room in between was Simon. The camera and Tom put the person on the ladder at that time. The rent ledger and the tenant list exposed the hidden letting, and Ellie’s messages the motive.
The date of a record takes on meaning next to the record that follows it: look at who entered the interval in which something left sound was broken. The person who dies is not always the target.
Deptford, 14 Ashgrove Road — 22–23 March 2029

The letting agent Simon Pryce was secretly letting rooms that appeared empty in Victor Crane’s houses and pocketing the rent. Ellie Ward, the tenant of no. 3, noticed and on 18 March threatened to tell the landlord. Afraid, Ellie left on 20 March, handing the room to her workmate Martin Hughes without telling anyone. On 22 March Simon took the key, removed the alarm’s battery and blocked the fire’s flue from outside with a cloth. He believed Ellie was sleeping in the room. That night Martin lit the fire and died.
Who is responsible for Martin’s death?
